# GN-Apex SDK — Full AI/Developer Reference

> **Status:** Production Reference
> **Package:** `@gnapex/sdk`
> **React Entry Point:** `@gnapex/sdk/react`
> **CLI:** `apex`, `nexus`
> **License:** MIT
> **Runtime:** Node.js >= 18
> **React Peer Dependency:** React 18.2+ or React 19

This document is the canonical developer and AI reference for the GN-Apex SDK.

It describes the public client APIs, React integrations, content engine, analytics engine, UI renderers, HTTP pipeline, push notifications, and CLI toolbelt.

AI coding assistants and developers should use this document as the primary reference when generating or modifying GN-Apex SDK integrations.

# Identity

GN-Apex SDK is the TypeScript/JavaScript client runtime for the GN-Apex platform.

The SDK provides a unified interface for applications that consume GN-Apex content, analytics, authentication, UI rendering, notifications, and platform services.

### Package

```text
@gnapex/sdk
```

### React Package

```text
@gnapex/sdk/react
```

### CLI Binaries

```text
apex
nexus
```

### Runtime

```text
Node.js >= 18
```

### License

```text
MIT
```

### React Compatibility

```text
React 18.2+
React 19
```

---

# Installation

Install the SDK through your package manager.

```bash
npm install @gnapex/sdk
```

Or:

```bash
pnpm add @gnapex/sdk
```

Or:

```bash
yarn add @gnapex/sdk
```

For React applications, the React entry point is available from:

```ts
import { useNexusAuth } from "@gnapex/sdk/react";
```

---

# Package Entry Points

The SDK exposes multiple entry points for different use cases.

## Main SDK

```ts
import { nexus, createNexusClient } from "@gnapex/sdk";
```

Use the main package for:

* GN-Apex client access
* Content APIs
* Analytics APIs
* Push notifications
* Core runtime functionality
* CLI-related SDK integration

## React SDK

```ts
import { useNexusAuth } from "@gnapex/sdk/react";
```

Use the React entry point for:

* Authentication hooks
* UI renderers
* Field renderers
* React-specific integrations

---

# Core Client

The GN-Apex SDK exposes a default zero-configuration client as well as a factory for creating isolated client instances.

## Zero-Configuration Singleton

```ts
import { nexus } from "@gnapex/sdk";

const page = await nexus.getPage("home");
```

The singleton client provides convenient access to the GN-Apex platform.

## Isolated Client Instance

```ts
import { createNexusClient } from "@gnapex/sdk";

const client = createNexusClient({
  projectId: "project-id",
  apiKey: "nx_pk_client_key",
  apiUrl: "https://api.gnapex.com",
});
```

Use `createNexusClient()` when an application requires an isolated configuration or multiple GN-Apex clients.

---

# Client Configuration

A client can be configured with the following core values:

```ts
const client = createNexusClient({
  projectId: "project-id",
  apiKey: "nx_pk_client_key",
  apiUrl: "https://api.gnapex.com",
});
```

### Configuration Fields

| Field       | Description                |
| ----------- | -------------------------- |
| `projectId` | GN-Apex project identifier |
| `apiKey`    | Client API key             |
| `apiUrl`    | GN-Apex API endpoint       |

Example:

```ts
const client = createNexusClient({
  projectId: "my-project",
  apiKey: "nx_pk_client_key",
  apiUrl: "https://api.gnapex.com",
});
```

---

# Content Engine API

The Content Engine provides access to GN-Apex-managed content.

The primary content APIs are:

* `getPage()`
* `getCollection()`
* `getGlobals()`
* `getItem()`
* `search()`

---

## Get Page

Fetch a page from GN-Apex.

### Convenience API

```ts
const page = await nexus.getPage("home");
```

### Content Namespace API

```ts
const page = await nexus.content.getPage<PageType>("home", {
  revalidate: 60,
  tags: ["content_home"],
  forceRefresh: false,
  includeMetadata: false,
});
```

### Options

```ts
{
  revalidate: 60,
  tags: ["content_home"],
  forceRefresh: false,
  includeMetadata: false
}
```

### Options Description

| Option            | Description                                  |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `revalidate`      | Revalidation interval in seconds, or `false` |
| `tags`            | Cache/content tags                           |
| `forceRefresh`    | Forces a fresh content request               |
| `includeMetadata` | Includes content metadata                    |

### Generic Type Support

The content result can be typed using TypeScript generics:

```ts
const page = await nexus.content.getPage<PageType>("home");
```

---

# Get Collection

Fetch a collection of content.

```ts
const posts = await nexus.content.getCollection<PostType>("posts", {
  page: 1,
  limit: 10,
  sort: "publishedAt",
  order: "desc",
  filter: {
    status: "published",
  },
  search: "release",
});
```

### Parameters

```text
collection
options
```

### Collection Options

| Option   | Example                   | Description            |
| -------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `page`   | `1`                       | Requested page         |
| `limit`  | `10`                      | Number of records      |
| `sort`   | `"publishedAt"`           | Field used for sorting |
| `order`  | `"desc"`                  | Sort direction         |
| `filter` | `{ status: "published" }` | Content filtering      |
| `search` | `"release"`               | Search query           |

### Example

```ts
const posts = await nexus.content.getCollection<PostType>("posts", {
  page: 1,
  limit: 10,
  sort: "publishedAt",
  order: "desc",
  filter: {
    status: "published",
  },
  search: "release",
});
```

---

# Get Globals

Fetch global platform content.

The globals API uses an options object rather than a key string.

```ts
const globals = await nexus.content.getGlobals({
  include: ["navigation", "footer", "theme"],
  revalidate: false,
});
```

### Options

| Option       | Description                               |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `include`    | List of global content groups to retrieve |
| `revalidate` | Cache revalidation configuration          |

Example:

```ts
const globals = await nexus.content.getGlobals({
  include: [
    "navigation",
    "footer",
    "theme",
  ],
  revalidate: false,
});
```

---

# Get Item

Fetch a single item from a collection by ID.

```ts
const item = await nexus.content.getItem<ItemType>(
  "posts",
  "item_123"
);
```

### Parameters

```text
collection
itemId
```

Example:

```ts
const item = await nexus.content.getItem<PostType>(
  "posts",
  "item_123"
);
```

---

# Search Content

Search across GN-Apex content.

The search API takes the query first and options second.

```ts
const results = await nexus.content.search<PostType>(
  "release notes",
  {
    collections: [
      "posts",
      "changelogs",
    ],
    limit: 20,
  }
);
```

### Search Options

| Option        | Description                        |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `collections` | Collections included in the search |
| `limit`       | Maximum number of results          |

### Example

```ts
const results = await nexus.content.search<PostType>(
  "release notes",
  {
    collections: ["posts", "changelogs"],
    limit: 20,
  }
);
```

---

# Analytics Engine API

The GN-Apex Analytics Engine provides application and user behavior tracking.

The analytics system supports automatic and manual tracking.

---

## Automatic Tracking

Automatic tracking monitors:

* Page views
* SPA navigation
* Clicks
* Dead clicks
* Rage clicks
* Scroll depth
* Web Vitals
* Errors

These events are monitored by the SDK's analytics runtime.

---

# Manual Tracking

Custom application events can be tracked manually.

```ts
nexus.analytics?.track(
  "button_click",
  {
    buttonId: "cta_hero",
  }
);
```

### Example

```ts
nexus.analytics?.track("button_click", {
  buttonId: "cta_hero",
});
```

Custom event properties can be supplied through the event payload.

---

# Identify

Associate analytics activity with a user.

```ts
await nexus.analytics?.identify(
  "usr_123",
  {
    email: "user@domain.com",
    plan: "pro",
  }
);
```

Example:

```ts
await nexus.analytics?.identify("usr_123", {
  email: "user@domain.com",
  plan: "pro",
});
```

---

# Group

Associate a user with an organization, account, or group.

```ts
await nexus.analytics?.group(
  "org_456",
  {
    tier: "enterprise",
  }
);
```

Example:

```ts
await nexus.analytics?.group("org_456", {
  tier: "enterprise",
});
```

---

# Alias

Create an analytics identity alias.

```ts
await nexus.analytics?.alias("usr_123");
```

---

# Purchase Tracking

Purchase events use a strict contract.

```ts
nexus.analytics?.trackPurchase({
  orderId: "ord_999",
  total: 129.99,
  revenue: 129.99,
  currency: "USD",
  products: [
    {
      id: "prod_1",
      name: "Pro Subscription",
      price: 129.99,
      quantity: 1,
      sku: "PRO-YEAR",
    },
  ],
});
```

### Purchase Fields

| Field      | Example     | Description             |
| ---------- | ----------- | ----------------------- |
| `orderId`  | `"ord_999"` | Unique order identifier |
| `total`    | `129.99`    | Order total             |
| `revenue`  | `129.99`    | Recorded revenue        |
| `currency` | `"USD"`     | Currency code           |
| `products` | `[...]`     | Purchased products      |

### Product Fields

```ts
{
  id: "prod_1",
  name: "Pro Subscription",
  price: 129.99,
  quantity: 1,
  sku: "PRO-YEAR"
}
```

---

# Session Control

Reset the analytics session or identity.

```ts
nexus.analytics?.reset(true);
```

Passing `true` requests a GDPR-compliant server scrub.

```ts
nexus.analytics?.reset(true);
```

---

# Authentication API

The React SDK provides authentication through the `useNexusAuth` hook.

Import it from:

```ts
import { useNexusAuth } from "@gnapex/sdk/react";
```

## Authentication Hook

```tsx
import { useNexusAuth } from "@gnapex/sdk/react";

function AuthComponent() {
  const {
    user,
    login,
    register,
    logout,
    updateProfile,
    isAuthenticated,
    isLoading,
    error,
  } = useNexusAuth();

  // ...
}
```

### Exposed Values

| Value             | Purpose                                 |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `user`            | Current authenticated user              |
| `login`           | Authentication/login operation          |
| `register`        | User registration operation             |
| `logout`          | Sign-out operation                      |
| `updateProfile`   | Update the authenticated user's profile |
| `isAuthenticated` | Authentication state                    |
| `isLoading`       | Authentication loading state            |
| `error`           | Authentication error state              |

---

# React UI & Field Renderers

GN-Apex provides reusable React components for rendering GN-Apex content and common field types.

Import these components from:

```ts
import {
  NexusRenderer,
  NexusRichText,
  NexusLongText,
  NexusIcon,
  NexusImage,
  NexusGallery,
  NexusVideo,
  NexusMap,
  NexusCode,
  NexusColor,
  NexusKeyValue,
  NexusTags,
  NexusProgress,
  NexusBoolean,
  NexusAddress,
  NexusGradient,
} from "@gnapex/sdk/react";
```

---

## NexusRenderer

Comprehensive document renderer.

```tsx
<NexusRenderer
  content={htmlString}
  hydrateCharts
  enableImageInteraction
/>
```

Features:

* Document rendering
* Built-in DOM sanitization
* SVG chart hydration
* Image interaction support

---

## NexusRichText

Specialized rich-text renderer.

```tsx
<NexusRichText
  value={htmlString}
  hydrateCharts
/>
```

---

## NexusLongText

Safe whitespace-preserving text renderer.

```tsx
<NexusLongText
  value={textString}
/>
```

---

## NexusIcon

Dynamic Lucide icon mapper.

```tsx
<NexusIcon
  name="ArrowRight"
  size={18}
/>
```

---

## NexusImage

Optimized image renderer.

```tsx
<NexusImage
  value={imgObjOrUrl}
  alt="Hero image"
/>
```

Features:

* Image URL/object support
* Lazy loading
* Alt text support

---

## NexusGallery

Responsive square-grid image gallery.

```tsx
<NexusGallery
  value={imgArray}
/>
```

---

## NexusVideo

Video renderer supporting multiple video sources.

```tsx
<NexusVideo
  value={videoUrl}
  autoplay={false}
/>
```

Supports:

* MP4
* YouTube
* Vimeo

---

## NexusMap

Interactive location map.

```tsx
<NexusMap
  value={{
    lat: 37.77,
    lng: -122.41,
    address: "San Francisco",
  }}
/>
```

---

## NexusCode

Code block renderer.

```tsx
<NexusCode
  value={codeString}
  language="typescript"
  showLineNumbers
/>
```

Features:

* Monospace code display
* Syntax language configuration
* Line numbers
* One-click clipboard copying

---

## NexusColor

Color value renderer.

```tsx
<NexusColor
  value="#00D4FF"
  showHexLabel
/>
```

---

## NexusKeyValue

Structured specification table.

```tsx
<NexusKeyValue
  value={{
    OS: "Linux",
    RAM: "32GB",
  }}
/>
```

---

## NexusTags

Tag badge list.

```tsx
<NexusTags
  value={[
    "Tech",
    "Release",
  ]}
/>
```

---

## NexusProgress

Progress indicator.

```tsx
<NexusProgress
  value={75}
  max={100}
/>
```

---

## NexusBoolean

Boolean/status renderer.

```tsx
<NexusBoolean
  value={true}
  trueLabel="Live"
  falseLabel="Draft"
/>
```

Provides a status badge with a pulsing indicator.

---

## NexusAddress

Address display card.

```tsx
<NexusAddress
  value={{
    street: "123 Main St",
    city: "Dar es Salaam",
  }}
/>
```

The component provides an address display with a map-pin icon.

---

## NexusGradient

Gradient container or masked-text renderer.

```tsx
<NexusGradient
  value="linear-gradient(...)"
  asTextMask
/>
```

The `asTextMask` option enables gradient text masking.

---

# HTTP Pipeline & Resilience

The SDK HTTP pipeline is exposed through:

```ts
nexus.http
```

The HTTP layer manages outgoing SDK requests.

---

## Request Headers

The SDK automatically injects:

```text
X-Nexus-Request-ID
X-Nexus-Client
X-Nexus-Project
```

### `X-Nexus-Request-ID`

Provides a request identifier for request tracing.

### `X-Nexus-Client`

Identifies the GN-Apex SDK client.

### `X-Nexus-Project`

Identifies the GN-Apex project associated with the request.

---

# Rate Limiting

The SDK HTTP pipeline uses the following client-side request limits:

```text
Normal mode: 100 requests/minute
Debug mode:  200 requests/minute
```

---

# Retry Strategy

The HTTP pipeline supports automatic retries.

The retry mechanism uses:

* Exponential backoff
* Jitter
* Maximum of 3 retries

The jitter helps prevent synchronized retry storms when multiple clients experience failures simultaneously.

---

# Circuit Breaker

The circuit breaker trips after:

```text
5 consecutive failures
```

The following failures count toward the circuit breaker:

* HTTP 5xx responses
* HTTP 429 responses
* Request timeouts

Client errors such as `404` do not trip the circuit breaker.

### Circuit-Breaker Rule

```text
5xx      → counts
429      → counts
Timeout  → counts
404      → ignored
Other 4xx client errors → ignored
```

---

# Push Notifications

The SDK provides a push notification client.

Import:

```ts
import { NexusPushClient } from "@gnapex/sdk";
```

Create a push client using the current GN-Apex configuration:

```ts
const push = new NexusPushClient(
  nexus.getConfig()
);
```

Request a push subscription:

```ts
await push.requestSubscription("/sw.js");
```

### Complete Example

```ts
import {
  nexus,
  NexusPushClient,
} from "@gnapex/sdk";

const push = new NexusPushClient(
  nexus.getConfig()
);

await push.requestSubscription("/sw.js");
```

The service-worker path is supplied to `requestSubscription()`.

---

# CLI Toolbelt

The GN-Apex CLI provides commands for local development, synchronization, validation, type generation, deployment, and diagnostics.

Available CLI commands:

```text
apex init
apex pull
apex push
apex diff
apex validate
apex types
apex studio
apex deploy
apex doctor
```

The CLI is available through the `apex` binary.

---

# CLI Command Reference

## `apex init`

Scaffold a GN-Apex environment and credentials.

```bash
npx apex init
```

Purpose:

* Initialize a GN-Apex project
* Scaffold the required environment
* Configure credentials

---

## `apex pull`

Download remote schema and content.

```bash
npx apex pull
```

Remote content is pulled into:

```text
.nexus/local/*.nx
```

---

## `apex push`

Upload and publish local schema and binary content.

```bash
npx apex push
```

Purpose:

* Upload local schema
* Upload local content
* Upload binary content
* Publish changes

---

## `apex diff`

Compare local state against the upstream origin.

```bash
npx apex diff
```

The comparison follows a Git-like diff model against:

```text
origin.nx
```

---

## `apex validate`

Validate local data against the local schema.

```bash
npx apex validate
```

The validation target is:

```text
schema.nx
```

---

## `apex types`

Generate TypeScript interfaces.

```bash
npx apex types
```

Generated interfaces are written to:

```text
types/nexus.d.ts
```

---

## `apex studio`

Start the local visual editor.

```bash
npx apex studio
```

The local Studio interface runs at:

```text
http://localhost:4646
```

---

## `apex deploy`

Build and transfer the deployment bundle to GN-Apex Edge.

```bash
npx apex deploy
```

The deployment workflow:

1. Builds the deployment bundle.
2. Transfers the bundle to GN-Apex Edge.

---

## `apex doctor`

Check SDK health and environment readiness.

```bash
npx apex doctor
```

Use this command when diagnosing:

* SDK environment problems
* Configuration issues
* Development environment readiness
* GN-Apex SDK health

---

# CLI Quick Reference

| Command             | Purpose                                 |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `npx apex init`     | Initialize environment and credentials  |
| `npx apex pull`     | Download remote schema and content      |
| `npx apex push`     | Upload and publish local schema/content |
| `npx apex diff`     | Compare local state with upstream       |
| `npx apex validate` | Validate local data against schema      |
| `npx apex types`    | Generate TypeScript interfaces          |
| `npx apex studio`   | Start local visual editor               |
| `npx apex deploy`   | Build and deploy to GN-Apex Edge        |
| `npx apex doctor`   | Diagnose SDK/environment readiness      |

---

# Production Usage Guidelines

## Use the SDK Package

Applications should import functionality from the documented public package entry points.

```ts
import { nexus } from "@gnapex/sdk";
```

React applications should use:

```ts
import { useNexusAuth } from "@gnapex/sdk/react";
```

---

## Use Isolated Clients When Required

When an application requires custom project configuration or multiple independent clients, use:

```ts
createNexusClient()
```

Example:

```ts
const client = createNexusClient({
  projectId: "project-id",
  apiKey: "nx_pk_client_key",
  apiUrl: "https://api.gnapex.com",
});
```

---

## Use TypeScript Generics

When the application knows the expected content shape, provide a TypeScript generic.

```ts
const page =
  await nexus.content.getPage<PageType>("home");
```

Collection example:

```ts
const posts =
  await nexus.content.getCollection<PostType>("posts");
```

Search example:

```ts
const results =
  await nexus.content.search<PostType>(
    "release notes"
  );
```

This allows application code to retain strong typing around content responses.

---

## Content Caching

The Content Engine supports revalidation options.

Example:

```ts
const page = await nexus.content.getPage("home", {
  revalidate: 60,
});
```

Disable revalidation where supported by using:

```ts
revalidate: false
```

Example:

```ts
const globals = await nexus.content.getGlobals({
  revalidate: false,
});
```

---

## Content Refresh

When fresh content is required, use:

```ts
forceRefresh: true
```

Example:

```ts
const page = await nexus.content.getPage("home", {
  forceRefresh: true,
});
```

---

# AI Coding Assistant Rules

This section is specifically intended for AI coding assistants such as:

* Claude
* ChatGPT
* GitHub Copilot
* Cursor
* Windsurf
* Other coding agents

AI assistants should treat this document as the primary GN-Apex SDK reference when this document corresponds to the installed SDK version.

---

## Rule 1 — Prefer Public APIs

Use documented public APIs such as:

```ts
nexus.content.getPage()
nexus.content.getCollection()
nexus.content.getGlobals()
nexus.content.getItem()
nexus.content.search()
```

Do not invent undocumented methods.

---

## Rule 2 — Preserve API Signatures

For content search, the query comes first:

```ts
nexus.content.search(
  "release notes",
  options
);
```

Do not reverse the arguments.

---

## Rule 3 — Globals Use an Options Object

Use:

```ts
nexus.content.getGlobals({
  include: ["navigation", "footer", "theme"],
});
```

Do not assume that globals require a string key argument unless the actual SDK version explicitly documents such an API.

---

## Rule 4 — Use Correct React Entry Point

React-specific APIs should be imported from:

```ts
@gnapex/sdk/react
```

Example:

```ts
import { useNexusAuth } from "@gnapex/sdk/react";
```

---

## Rule 5 — Preserve Type Safety

When content types are known, use generics:

```ts
nexus.content.getPage<PageType>("home");
```

rather than unnecessarily falling back to untyped values.

---

## Rule 6 — Do Not Invent Component Props

Only use documented props unless the installed SDK source/types explicitly confirm additional properties.

For example:

```tsx
<NexusImage
  value={imgObjOrUrl}
  alt="Hero image"
/>
```

Do not invent unsupported properties.

---

## Rule 7 — Preserve Analytics Contracts

Purchase tracking must follow the documented structure:

```ts
nexus.analytics?.trackPurchase({
  orderId: "ord_999",
  total: 129.99,
  revenue: 129.99,
  currency: "USD",
  products: [
    {
      id: "prod_1",
      name: "Pro Subscription",
      price: 129.99,
      quantity: 1,
      sku: "PRO-YEAR",
    },
  ],
});
```

---

## Rule 8 — Respect Optional Analytics

The SDK examples use optional chaining:

```ts
nexus.analytics?.track(...)
```

and:

```ts
await nexus.analytics?.identify(...)
```

Preserve this behavior when working with code that treats analytics as optional.

---

## Rule 9 — Do Not Bypass the HTTP Pipeline

SDK requests should use the SDK's HTTP pipeline where the corresponding SDK API provides that behavior.

The HTTP pipeline is responsible for:

* Request identification
* Client identification
* Project identification
* Rate limiting
* Retries
* Backoff
* Circuit breaking

---

## Rule 10 — Respect Runtime Requirements

The SDK requires:

```text
Node.js >= 18
```

React integrations require:

```text
React 18.2+
React 19
```

AI-generated integrations should not intentionally target unsupported runtime versions.

---

# Compatibility

## Node.js

Minimum supported runtime:

```text
Node.js 18
```

Therefore:

```text
Node.js >= 18
```

---

## React

Supported React versions:

```text
React 18.2+
React 19
```

---

## TypeScript

The SDK is designed for TypeScript/JavaScript applications.

TypeScript users should take advantage of the generic content APIs:

```ts
getPage<PageType>()
getCollection<PostType>()
getItem<ItemType>()
search<PostType>()
```

---

# Complete Integration Example

The following example demonstrates a basic GN-Apex content integration:

```ts
import {
  nexus,
  createNexusClient,
} from "@gnapex/sdk";

interface Post {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  publishedAt: string;
}

const client = createNexusClient({
  projectId: "project-id",
  apiKey: "nx_pk_client_key",
  apiUrl: "https://api.gnapex.com",
});

async function loadContent() {
  const page =
    await client.content.getPage("home", {
      revalidate: 60,
      tags: ["content_home"],
      forceRefresh: false,
      includeMetadata: false,
    });

  const posts =
    await client.content.getCollection<Post>(
      "posts",
      {
        page: 1,
        limit: 10,
        sort: "publishedAt",
        order: "desc",
        filter: {
          status: "published",
        },
      }
    );

  return {
    page,
    posts,
  };
}
```

---

# Complete Analytics Example

```ts
import { nexus } from "@gnapex/sdk";

async function trackUserActivity() {
  nexus.analytics?.track(
    "button_click",
    {
      buttonId: "cta_hero",
    }
  );

  await nexus.analytics?.identify(
    "usr_123",
    {
      email: "user@domain.com",
      plan: "pro",
    }
  );

  await nexus.analytics?.group(
    "org_456",
    {
      tier: "enterprise",
    }
  );
}
```

---

# Complete Purchase Example

```ts
import { nexus } from "@gnapex/sdk";

function trackPurchase() {
  nexus.analytics?.trackPurchase({
    orderId: "ord_999",
    total: 129.99,
    revenue: 129.99,
    currency: "USD",
    products: [
      {
        id: "prod_1",
        name: "Pro Subscription",
        price: 129.99,
        quantity: 1,
        sku: "PRO-YEAR",
      },
    ],
  });
}
```

---

# Complete React Authentication Example

```tsx
import { useNexusAuth } from "@gnapex/sdk/react";

export function AuthComponent() {
  const {
    user,
    login,
    register,
    logout,
    updateProfile,
    isAuthenticated,
    isLoading,
    error,
  } = useNexusAuth();

  if (isLoading) {
    return <div>Loading...</div>;
  }

  if (!isAuthenticated) {
    return (
      <div>
        <button onClick={() => login()}>
          Login
        </button>

        <button onClick={() => register()}>
          Register
        </button>
      </div>
    );
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <p>
        Welcome {user?.email}
      </p>

      <button onClick={() => logout()}>
        Logout
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

---

# Complete Push Notification Example

```ts
import {
  nexus,
  NexusPushClient,
} from "@gnapex/sdk";

async function enablePushNotifications() {
  const push = new NexusPushClient(
    nexus.getConfig()
  );

  await push.requestSubscription(
    "/sw.js"
  );
}
```

---

# CLI Quick Start

Initialize a project:

```bash
npx apex init
```

Pull remote content:

```bash
npx apex pull
```

Validate local content:

```bash
npx apex validate
```

Generate TypeScript types:

```bash
npx apex types
```

Compare local and remote state:

```bash
npx apex diff
```

Start GN-Apex Studio:

```bash
npx apex studio
```

Push changes:

```bash
npx apex push
```

Deploy:

```bash
npx apex deploy
```

Run diagnostics:

```bash
npx apex doctor
```

---

# API Summary

## Core

```ts
nexus
createNexusClient()
```

## Content

```ts
nexus.getPage()
nexus.content.getPage()
nexus.content.getCollection()
nexus.content.getGlobals()
nexus.content.getItem()
nexus.content.search()
```

## Analytics

```ts
nexus.analytics?.track()
nexus.analytics?.identify()
nexus.analytics?.group()
nexus.analytics?.alias()
nexus.analytics?.trackPurchase()
nexus.analytics?.reset()
```

## Authentication

```ts
useNexusAuth()
```

## Rendering

```tsx
<NexusRenderer />
<NexusRichText />
<NexusLongText />
<NexusIcon />
<NexusImage />
<NexusGallery />
<NexusVideo />
<NexusMap />
<NexusCode />
<NexusColor />
<NexusKeyValue />
<NexusTags />
<NexusProgress />
<NexusBoolean />
<NexusAddress />
<NexusGradient />
```

## Push

```ts
NexusPushClient
```

## CLI

```bash
apex init
apex pull
apex push
apex diff
apex validate
apex types
apex studio
apex deploy
apex doctor
```

# Stability & Reference Policy

This document should describe the **actual public SDK contract**.

When updating the SDK:

1. Update this reference when a public API changes.
2. Keep examples synchronized with the implementation.
3. Do not document APIs that do not exist in the released package.
4. Do not remove existing API documentation without confirming a breaking change.
5. Keep TypeScript signatures synchronized with the published type declarations.
6. Keep CLI commands synchronized with the actual CLI.
7. Update compatibility requirements when runtime support changes.
8. Clearly document breaking changes.
9. Keep authentication, analytics, content, and rendering contracts explicit.
10. Treat the published SDK types and implementation as the final verification source when this document and the installed package differ.

---

# Versioning

The SDK follows semantic versioning:

```text
MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
```

Changes should be classified appropriately:

* **MAJOR** — breaking API changes
* **MINOR** — backward-compatible functionality
* **PATCH** — backward-compatible fixes

When a breaking API change occurs, this document should be updated to reflect the new contract.
